metaTitle: Pest Control Advertising: Google Ads, LSA and Meta
metaDescription: Pest control advertising run against booked jobs: Google Search Ads, Local Services Ads and Meta, in ad accounts you own. Ad spend is paid to the platforms.

hero.h1: Pest Control Advertising Tracked to Booked Jobs
hero.subhead: Reach homeowners the moment they search for pest help, then trace your ad spend to booked jobs. ASP runs Google Ads, Local Services Ads and Meta for you.
points: Ad accounts set up in your name
Spend paid straight to Google and Meta

why.heading: Why pest control companies run paid search
why.intro: Organic rankings take months. Ads put your company in front of buyers searching right now, and they stop when the budget stops, so every dollar has to be tracked.

cards.title: Pay per lead on LSA
cards.body: Local Services Ads charge per lead instead of per click, and the placement sits above the map results.

cards.title: Catch the specific problem
cards.body: Search Ads reach the homeowner typing a specific pest problem into Google, with one ad group per service so you can see which line pays.

cards.title: Answer the careful buyer
cards.body: A 2005 EPA fact sheet's questions for homeowners include licensing, appropriate insurance and guarantees. Ads that answer those up front give buyers fewer reasons to keep shopping.

services.heading: Pest control ad channels ASP manages
services.intro: Each channel gets its own line in the report, down to cost per booked job.

cards.title: Local Services Ads
cards.body: Google screens every business before ads run. We then manage the signals it ranks on, including your bid, rating, review count, response time and photos.

cards.title: Google Search Ads
cards.body: Phrase match, one ad group per service or service area, and a negative keyword list we add to every week.

cards.title: Clean account settings
cards.body: Search partners off, display off on search campaigns, location set to presence, and branded searches in their own campaign.

cards.title: Meta retargeting
cards.body: Cold ads asking strangers to book rarely work for the trades, so Meta here retargets site visitors and carries seasonal offers.

cards.title: Recruiting campaigns
cards.body: Hiring technicians runs as its own Meta campaign with its own budget, kept apart from lead-generation numbers.

cards.title: Tracking to booked jobs
cards.body: Calls tracked by source, tagged forms, LSA leads checked monthly against Google's billing, and, if you use Housecall Pro, booked revenue sent to Google Ads as offline conversions.

process.heading: How we launch your pest control ads

steps.title: Fix tracking first
steps.body: Calls, forms and your CRM get wired so each ad dollar can be traced to a booked job.

steps.title: Set budget from job value
steps.body: Spend is sized from the value of a booked pest job, then adjusted as real job data comes in.

steps.title: Launch LSA and Search
steps.body: Local Services Ads go first if you pass screening and your reviews can support it, with Search Ads covering specific problems.

steps.title: Read your own data
steps.body: Budget and ad schedule follow your account and job data, not a national calendar.

pricing.heading: Packages for pest control advertising
pricing.subhead: For pest control companies, paid media management is included from Growth up, covering Google Ads, Meta and LSA. Ad spend is paid to the platforms from your own accounts.

faqs.question: Is pest control eligible for Local Services Ads?
faqs.answer: Yes. Google lists pest control services as an eligible Local Services Ads category in the US, and you need to pass its screening first. Google sets those requirements and can change them.

faqs.question: Why run Search Ads if we already run LSA?
faqs.answer: Because LSA inventory is capped per metro, and Search lets you target the specific problems people type. Most companies running paid seriously run both.

faqs.question: How much should a pest control company spend on ads?
faqs.answer: There is no flat number that fits every company. Start from what a booked job is worth to you. Ad spend goes straight to Google or Meta and is separate from our management fee.

faqs.question: Do Facebook ads work for pest control?
faqs.answer: For retargeting and seasonal offers on recurring services, they can. We run Meta alongside search, not in place of it.

faqs.question: Will you change my conversion action to exit the learning phase faster?
faqs.answer: No. Switching to a softer event like a page view makes the dashboard look better and changes nothing on your schedule. We use geography, budget weighting, ad count and creative instead.

faqs.question: Should pest control ad budgets rise in summer?
faqs.answer: Not on a national calendar alone. BLS figures show about 12% more people on pest control payrolls in July 2024 than in January 2024, but that isn't ad demand. Your budget follows your own account and job data.

faqs.question: How do you track Local Services Ads leads for pest control?
faqs.answer: Each LSA lead is tagged as LSA in your CRM and checked every month against Google's LSA billing. That lets the report show cost per booked job for LSA next to your other channels.
